clue.text: Part of service delivering freight by order

indicators.note: delivering read as freeing or releasing the letters, so the word freight is set loose and rearranged

parts.note: to order is to command

explanation.surface: A section of a delivery service ships goods as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivering' releases FREIGHT into FIGHTER; 'by' is a link. Fighter Command was the RAF's air-defence arm in the Second World War, so the service is the air force, not a parcel firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighter Command was one branch of the Royal Air Force, so it is a component of an armed service.

clue.text: Victoire! Door opens — West door, actually

parts.note: victoire is the French word for a win, so the exclamation is a French win

indicators.note: opens read as the word door losing the two letters that form the conjunction or, leaving just its opening

explanation.surface: A French cry of triumph as a door swings open to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' takes OR out of DOOR to leave DO. The definition says 'actually' because this so-called window is really a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A French window is a glazed pair of doors opening onto a garden, a door in fact despite its name.

clue.text: Seek information which may be mixed

definitions.meaning: to question someone closely, as police do a suspect
a cooked dish of assorted meats, the mixed version of a broiled plate

explanation.definitionFit: To grill is to interrogate, and a mixed grill is a plate of assorted grilled meats.

clue.text: Gas disperser is model of listener: he will …

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
the ear is the organ that listens
is contracted to an apostrophe S
he will contracts to he'll

explanation.surface: A gas weapon described as a model ear, with the clue running on to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts run T, EAR, 'S (from 'is', placed after the ear), HE'LL; the dots carry the sentence into 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear shell is an artillery round that releases tear gas, so it spreads gas over an area.

clue.text: … abandon silence for Ruth

indicators.note: for signals swapping one word for its synonym: rend in place of tear, both meaning rip
abandon tells us to drop the letters that follow from the shell

parts.note: the dots carry over the answer to 3 down, the gas-dispersing shell
SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A man must give up keeping quiet for the sake of a woman named Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: Starting from 3 down, 'abandon silence' removes SH, and 'for' swaps TEAR for its synonym REND, leaving REND + ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth Rendell was a celebrated English crime novelist, so the first name points to her surname.

clue.text: Food in the 10 with 3 (part 2)s eaten amid 3 (part 1)s

definitions.text: Food in the 10 with 3 (part 2)s eaten amid 3 (part 1)s

parts.words: Food in the 10 with 3 (part 2)s eaten amid 3 (part 1)s
parts.note: the Walrus and the Carpenter in Through the Looking-Glass eat shellfish in their shells while the Walrus weeps tears over them

explanation.walkthrough: 10 is LOOKING GLASS; 3 down is TEAR SHELL, so part 2 is SHELL and part 1 is TEAR: shelled food eaten amid tears.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's poem the Walrus and the Carpenter eat the little shellfish they have lured from the sea, weeping as they do.

clue.text: How 13 part of 16 laid claim to daughter of …

definitions.text: How 13 part of 16 laid claim to daughter of …

parts.words: How 13 part of 16 laid claim to daughter of …
parts.note: the White Knight, a knight like the Red one, repeatedly boasts that each gadget is something he devised himself; necessity is proverbially the mother of such contrivances

explanation.walkthrough: 13 is WHITE and 16 is RED KNIGHT, so 'part of 16' is KNIGHT. 'Necessity is the mother of invention', so its daughter is invention; the dots run into 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's White Knight introduces each of his odd contraptions with this boast of personal authorship.

clue.text: … marshal keeping piano out of sink, which can't be helped

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

indicators.note: the letter for piano is taken out of the other word

parts.note: a cesspit is a sink of filth
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: An official kept a piano from falling into a drain, which was unavoidable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes P from CESSPIT to leave CESSIT, and 'keeping' puts that inside NEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be helped is a matter of compulsion, an unavoidable need.

clue.text: Is life in Italy musical?

parts.note: e is the Italian word for is
vita is Italian for life; 'in Italy' tells us both words are Italian

explanation.surface: A question about whether Italian life is like a show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Italy' applies to 'Is' as well as 'life': both are translated into Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Enterprising fellow — as such, with change of pole, holding capital

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other
one compass pole, south, gives way to the other, north, within the word such

parts.note: Oslo is the capital of Norway

explanation.surface: A go-getter, so called, who switches poles while gripping some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with change of pole' turns the S of SUCH into N for NUCH; 'holding' puts OSLO inside after the N. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no slouch is energetic and capable, the opposite of a lazy idler.

clue.text: Reverser's convenience, like horse heard by girl

parts.note: a public convenience is a lavatory, a loo
kin as an adjective means related or alike, as in akin

indicators.note: heard signals that the word for a horse is said aloud and written as what it sounds like

parts.note: gee-gee is a child's word for a horse
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A toilet used by someone who goes backwards, like a horse a girl listens to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns GEE-GEE into the letters GG it sounds like. A mirror shows everything reversed, which gives 'Reverser'; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror shows every image back to front, so it reverses left and right.

clue.text: Lost Mary's instrument

definitions.meaning: the Mary ... was the ship found abandoned in 1872 with its crew gone
a keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal plates, also spelt celesta

explanation.definitionFit: The Mary Celeste is the famous lost-crew ship, and the celeste is a bell-toned keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Eagles to represent Che

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Birds of prey are chosen to stand for a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The innocent-looking 'to' is part of the answer; 'represent' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Che Guevara's first name was Ernesto; Che was a nickname.

clue.text: Success in the Guardian came from much reflection

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself editorially as we
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A triumph in the newspaper resulted from deep thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' is light, not thought: an object looks this colour because it reflects all wavelengths.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface appears this colour when it reflects nearly all the light falling on it.

clue.text: See 6
CD disguised as red silk

indicators.note: disguised means made to look different, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A compact disc dressed up to look like a piece of red fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser disk is an optical disc read by laser, of which the compact disc is the best-known kind.

clue.text: Not the one in the 10 correct, including Ken D(odd)

indicators.note: including means taking something inside

parts.note: correct means right

indicators.note: odd signals the letters are jumbled, while the brackets make Ken Dodd the comedian

explanation.surface: Being right about Ken Dodd, the comedian, written with a strange bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' jumbles KEND into EDKN, which 'including' puts after the R of RIGHT. The White Knight is the knight in the book everyone remembers; this one is his rival.
explanation.definitionFit: In Through the Looking-Glass the Red Knight fights the White Knight, so he is the other knight in the story.

clue.text: Writing missive not finished after half a month

indicators.note: after places the cut letter behind the half month
half of the month's name is kept, its second half dropped

parts.note: November is a month

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: Composing an unfinished letter some way into a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts NOVEMBER to NOVE; 'not finished' cuts LETTER to LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, a piece of writing.

clue.text: Is Parisian intact in church law?

annotationWithheld.why: Is Parisian intact in church law? (4,3): EST inside TACT, where 'intact' must be split as 'in tact', so the one word is both the container indicator and the TACT fodder, which the check refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: Is Parisian intact in church law?

clue.text: Great ship's quarters with flower put in

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: E and N are compass quarters, east and north
an aster is a flower

explanation.surface: Accommodation on a big vessel decorated with a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Eastern was Brunel's huge Victorian steamship; the answer completes its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel's giant steamship was called the Great Eastern, so this is the second word of its name.

clue.text: Am assuredly desirous of being the respected senior

parts.note: emphatic do, as in I do want, stands for am assuredly
to yen is to long for

explanation.surface: Claiming to really wish to become the honoured elder.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior and respected member of a group.

clue.text: Volume of traffic?

definitions.meaning: a book collecting several works in one binding
the full old name of a bus, a vehicle in road traffic

explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a collected edition in one volume, and the full name of a bus.

clue.text: Having spirit without energy, I need a pancake

indicators.note: without means losing the following letters

parts.note: a goblin is a mischievous spirit
go means energy, as in full of go

explanation.surface: Someone who is lively but tired needs a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'need' are links; 'without' removes GO from GOBLIN to leave BLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes, served with caviar or soured cream.

clue.text: Offensive weapon as flood defence

definitions.meaning: a sand-filled bag used as a cosh
a bag of sand piled up to hold back water

explanation.definitionFit: A sandbag is both a cosh for attacking someone and a barrier stacked against floods.

clue.text: Batman starts cattle disease

indicators.note: starts means only the opening letters of the word are kept

parts.note: brucellosis is a bacterial disease of cattle

explanation.surface: The caped crusader begins a disease of cows.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman's real identity is Bruce Wayne.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman's alter ego is the millionaire Bruce Wayne.

clue.text: Report of dreamy Walter's walk causes temper

indicators.note: report of signals a phrase said aloud

parts.note: Walter Mitty is Thurber's daydreamer, and a gait is a way of walking

explanation.surface: An account of how a daydreamer strolls leads to anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' is the verb meaning to moderate, not anger; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or moderate it.

clue.text: Leave posh American lawman with cheese

parts.note: to leave is to go
U means upper-class
a DA is an American district attorney

explanation.surface: Depart the smart US prosecutor holding some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild Dutch cheese.

clue.text: Vague quality of natural impulse surrounding princess's head

indicators.note: surrounding means placed around the other piece

parts.note: an instinct is a natural impulse
Di was Diana, Princess of Wales
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Gut feeling around the head of a princess makes for blur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is the headland NESS, not the first letter of 'princess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indistinctness is the state of being unclear or blurred.
